items.notes: Floor hatch into a one-person lock-out chamber below the deck, just aft of the map table, so the crew can read the table and step straight out. Climb down, seal the top hatch, flood, open the bottom hatch to the sea; the pumps are loud. Placed for play, not engineering realism.
Up into the conning tower and its top hatch
Orders and dive status, above the bulkhead hatch.

compartments.notes: The pilot's bubble: one unbroken acrylic hemisphere about 2.2 m across with a heavy steel ring at its rim, the pilot alone on the centreline with glass all round and below, a hand's width from armrest to glass.

The crowded catch-all and the crew's hub. Starboard: the sonar desk just aft of the dome ring, then countermeasures. Port: the map table in a bay in the hull wall, its operator standing at the middle of the front edge, observers standing either side. Then the lock-out trunk in the floor, and the conning-tower ladder and lockers by the bulkhead. Countermeasures and the map table face each other across the aisle.
Watertight hatch, which can isolate a flooding engineering space.
The mechanic's end of the boat, louder and lower as the hull tapers. Engine and power, life support, ballast, the bilge well and the drop-weight release: every hands-on utility job, tightly packed.
